question: A car traveling at a speed of 50 km/hour can complete a journey in 8 hours. How long will it take to travel the same distance at 40 km/hour?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the distance is constant, Speed and Time are inversely proportional.

Ratio of Speeds (S₁ : S₂) = 50 : 40 = 5 : 4

Ratio of Times (T₁ : T₂) = 4 : 5

Given 4 units = 8 hours ⇒ 1 unit = 2 hours.

Required Time (5 units) = 5 × 2 = 10 h.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the car (S₁) = 50 km/h

Time taken (T₁) = 8 h

New speed (S₂) = 40 km/h

 
• 
 
 
 Total Distance = 400 km
 
 
 Case 1: Speed = 50 km/h | Time = 8 h
 
 
 Case 2: Speed = 40 km/h | Time = ?

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 50 × 8 = 400 km

⇒ Time taken at 40 km/h = 400 ÷ 40

⇒ Time taken = 10 h

**∴ The correct answer is 10 h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

When equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, the Average Speed for the entire journey is given by (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

If two objects are moving in opposite directions with speeds x and y, their relative speed is (x + y). If they move in the same direction, it is (x − y).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.
